task.title: Implement runtime context-boundary dispatch
task.summary: Implement generic runtime-owned session/context-boundary dispatch and source-backed context packets so compaction, fresh gate evaluation, parallel continuation, and future subagents use trace/source refs instead of canonical roles.

goal.outcome: Runtime can request and record role-free source-backed context boundaries for compaction, fresh gate evaluation, parallel continuation, and adapter-backed subagent spawning, with high-signal packets and content evidence requirements.
acceptance: Runtime dispatch/request model uses context-boundary reason, trace/task/sprint scope, graph lens, expected output, constraints, source refs, artifact status, budgets, and content-evidence requirements; role is absent or optional compatibility metadata only.

Source-backed context packet generation points agents to current trace/scope, graph lens, exact source refs, blockers, artifact status, expected output, constraints, and content-evidence requirements without including full chat history, full graph dumps, or unrelated roadmap work.
Fresh gate evaluation handoff can be requested through runtime context-boundary dispatch and records platform-limited evidence when the host cannot spawn a fresh session.
Existing same-session compaction and /wiki-resume --new paths consume the same source-backed packet contract where compatible.
Artifact status and worktree isolation remain enforced before write-capable spawned/continued sessions; role labels do not determine conflicts, permissions, or gate criteria.
Gateway preflight/reporting treats freshness as context-boundary plus content evidence, not validator compatibility label.

TASK-specific tests cover packet shape, dispatch-ready vs platform-limited outcomes, fresh gate handoff, context-bloat continuation, compatibility role labels not being required, and no validation/publish loop root.
non_goals: Do not remove existing role fields from public/compatibility schemas unless a compatibility-safe optional facade is provided.
Do not change public tool schemas except compatibility-safe additions or optional fields.
Do not create src/validation, src/publish, or src/publication roots.
Do not bypass gate reports, artifact leases, content evidence requirements, or publication approval.
Do not publish, push, or run destructive cleanup.

loop_start.reason: Compiler loops start from CodeWiki source refs; agents may refresh context when chat is noisy, stale, or token-heavy.

validation.reason: Implementation validation must not reuse builder thought context and must cite checked content proof.

next_loop.reason: The next gateway must independently validate implementation evidence and cite checked content proof.

closure_brief.user_intent: Proceed with checkpoint-aware CodeWiki context projection to reduce chat noise while keeping Pi primitives.
implemented_changes: Added a CodeWiki Pi context hook that injects one current source-backed context projection before each provider request.
Removed repeated old CodeWiki kickoff/context-refresh packets from LLM-visible context.
Pruned raw chat only after a stable durable checkpoint before the latest user/custom prompt.
Preserved active tool-call/tool-result working sets and uncheckpointed user nuance.
Kept Pi primitives for session, compaction, transformContext, and new-session lifecycle.
acceptance_evidence: wiki_audit lexicon/source-contract/alignment/changed scoped TASK-121 passed except known graph/generated warnings.
non_goals_preserved: Did not replace Pi session, compaction, or transformContext primitives.
Did not prune active tool-result turns after latest user prompt.
Did not remove legacy role fields or make role a scheduling criterion.
Did not publish, push, or run destructive cleanup.
remaining_risks: Independent implementation validation still required before task close.

risks: Context hook builds resume context with refresh=false and a short cache; if generated graph is stale, projection can be stale until CodeWiki refresh runs.
Projection must remain conservative around active tool-result turns to avoid breaking provider tool-call grammar.
